single.rationale: Tredegar returned to profitability in 2025 after two years of losses, generating positive free cash flow and improving operating metrics. However, significant headwinds remain: aluminum extrusion orders declined 23.6% after tariff increases to 50%, structural challenges persist from tariff inversions favoring imports of finished goods, and High Performance Films faces customer concentration risk (top 4 customers = 88% of segment sales). The company operates in cyclical, commoditized markets with limited pricing power and faces ongoing regulatory pressures.

team.thesis: Tredegar operates two segments: Aluminum Extrusions (86% of consolidated net sales in 2025) producing soft and medium strength aluminum extrusions for building & construction, automotive, consumer durables, and other markets, and High Performance Films (14% of 2025 net sales) producing surface protection films primarily for flat panel and flexible displays.

dropped.claim: Tredegar returned to profitability in FY2025 with net income of $33.5M after two years of losses, driven by Aluminum Extrusions (86% of sales) volume growth of 12.9% and improved cash generation (operating cash flow of $33.0M, free cash flow of $15.7M). However, the business faces severe near-term headwinds: weekly net new orders in Aluminum Extrusions collapsed 23.6% after June 2025 tariff increases (from 3.4 to 2.6 million pounds per week), open orders 'fall below normalized levels' per management, and structural tariff inversion allows foreign finished goods to undercut domestic producers despite 50% Section 232 tariffs. High Performance Films (14% of sales) saw EBITDA decline $3.3M to $27.1M with 88% customer concentration in four customers. The balance sheet improved materially (long-term debt reduced from $60.6M to $34.5M, net debt only $27.8M), but R&D spending collapsed from $5.3M in 2022 to $702,000 in 2025, and operational fragility is evident from $2.2M in weather/equipment-related maintenance costs in H1 2025.
